static_traits.name: Li Hang
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents; there is tension and conflict in the family because of his unwillingness to work and lack of motivation
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends, mainly interacting around video games; finds it difficult to discuss feelings about work and productivity with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior psychotherapy or related intervention
static_traits.language_features: Neutral tone; clear expression, able to give examples and self-reflect; able to describe specific triggering situations and subjective experiences

basic_info.main_problem: I don't want to work, because I feel it is a form of control, and I will always struggle financially and produce nothing. These thoughts began in my early twenties and gradually worsened after difficulties finding work and pressure from family to be independent; I lack motivation to look for work, and the thoughts appear daily, especially when my parents mention job hunting. I try to distract myself with video games, but the thoughts persist.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling now because I realize these negative thoughts are limiting my potential and causing conflicts within my family. I want to stop these negative self-labeling thoughts, enjoy my activities again, and stop constantly feeling like I am failing.
growth_experiences: In his early 20s, he experienced difficulties finding a job and pressure from his family to be independent, and first developed the negative thought that 'work equals control, and I will always be poor and unproductive'. The stress level was initially high; afterwards these thoughts gradually became more frequent and more intense, which weakened his motivation to be employed and his willingness to seek work.

A few months ago, I accidentally scratched a water ski while taking it off a truck; since then, whenever a minor mistake occurs (such as spilling coffee on the desk last week), I quickly engage in self-deprecation and negative labeling ('I am so stupid', 'I am so incompetent', 'I am so careless'). These thoughts ruin my mood for the whole day, reduce my focus and enjoyment of activities, and reinforce the cognitive rule of 'minor mistake = total failure'.

core_beliefs: Work will deprive me of my autonomy (work is control)
I will always be poor and unproductive

special_situations.event: When parents bring up the topic of job hunting or urge independence
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I go to work, I will be controlled; even if I start working, I will always struggle financially and have no output, unable to change the current situation
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing employment with the parents; does not look for work, distracting attention with video games
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Work will control me, I am doomed to be poor forever and have no output

special_situations.event: In one's twenties, facing job-search setbacks and difficulty finding work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot find a job quickly, it means I am no good, I have failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces or stops active job-seeking actions, rationalizing with the belief 'I am not capable anyway'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot find a suitable job, I will keep failing in the future too

special_situations.event: After everyday small mistakes (such as scratching a paddleboard, spilling coffee on the table)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any small mistake means I am incompetent overall; I must make no mistakes to prove I have value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Harsh self-criticism and negative labeling, constraining the self with high standards to avoid making mistakes again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am stupid, I am incompetent

special_situations.event: When a mistake is seen by others or realizing others may evaluate oneself
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others see my mistakes, they will surely think I am incompetent; others' evaluations determine my worth
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids talking with friends about feelings concerning work and productivity, reducing exposure to others' evaluations

core_conflict.wish: Longs for autonomy and not being controlled, able to freely choose his lifestyle and way of working
core_conflict.fear: Fears being controlled by others or the system, and fears being seen as incompetent and a failure and thereby losing value
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control by avoiding work and job seeking, reducing shame and anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: A self that is incompetent, prone to failure, and needs to avoid being judged
object_relations.object_representation: The controlling and critical other (such as parents, the workplace)

object_relations.self_representation: A child required to be independent and prone to being judged
object_relations.object_representation: Parents who are strict and emphasize independence and work

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When parents mention job hunting or urge him to become independent soon
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiences parents as controllers, believing that suggestions equal deprivation of autonomy (transference)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes that 'work is control', rejects suggestions with firm declarative statements, quickly shifts the topic to video games, with a resolute tone but avoids in-depth discussion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When small mistakes of his own (such as spilling coffee) are mentioned in life or in sessions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes others will see him as incompetent, and immediately turns negative emotions into self-attack
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses strongly self-blaming statements (such as 'I am so stupid'), dismisses positive feedback, with a low tone and reduced eye contact.

manifestations: Viewing work as external control over oneself
Producing resistance and avoidance in situations of family demands for independence and work
Maintaining a subjective sense of autonomy by not working
outcomes: Lacking job-search motivation and long-term unemployment
Intensifying conflict and stress with parents
Decreased sense of responsibility in life

manifestations: Believing one will always be poor and unproductive
Daily life revolving around video games, difficulty carrying out self-care and taking responsibility

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Using rigid rules such as 'I must not make mistakes'
Directly equating not making mistakes with personal worth

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: After a small mistake, assumes 'everyone thinks I am incompetent'
Projecting one's self-evaluation onto how others see oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent negative self-labeling and severe self-blame
Caring excessively about others' evaluations, cautiously avoiding mistakes

positive_force: Possesses self-awareness, recognizes that negative thoughts limit potential, and proactively seeks help
Able to clearly describe triggering situations of the problem (such as parents bringing up work, small daily mistakes)
Maintains contact with a few friends; has some social support
negative_force: Views work as control and makes catastrophic predictions about the future
Black-and-white perfectionist rules, small mistakes mean total negation
Overgeneralization and personalization reinforce the failure self-schema
Avoiding employment and emotions through video games, decline in sense of responsibility and self-care
Strained relationship with parents; external pressure intensifies inner conflict

antecedent: Parents bring up finding a job or urge independence
Thinking about the demands of employment and independence
target_behavior.core_reason: Equates work with being controlled, and catastrophically predicts being perpetually poor and unproductive
target_behavior.function: Escaping the potential discomfort of being controlled and failing, gaining a temporary sense of autonomy
target_behavior.consequence: Long-term unemployment, financial instability, intensified conflict with parents, and impaired daily responsibilities and self-care

antecedent: Everyday small mishaps (such as scratching the paddleboard or spilling coffee)
Realizing others may have noticed one's mistake
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized rigid perfectionist rule (must not make mistakes), generalizing small errors into overall incompetence
target_behavior.function: Attempts to maintain control and prevent further mistakes through self-punishment, or to lower in advance the threat of others' criticism
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, impaired attention, reduced enjoyment of activities, and further avoidance of interaction and challenges
